fields.name: relevance_to_review_question
fields.description: Whether the paper provides substantive evidence relevant to applications of large language models in urban planning and smart cities within the urban planning and smart cities domain, based only on the title and abstract.

fields.name: datasets_used
fields.description: Datasets, corpora, benchmarks, or data sources used to develop, train, test, or evaluate the LLM-based approach.
fields.example: City complaint dataset; traffic sensor records; manually annotated urban planning documents

fields.name: methods
fields.description: The LLM-based method, model architecture, prompting strategy, pipeline, or system design used in the study.
fields.example: Multi-LLM scoring framework with prompt-based classification and benchmark construction

fields.name: key_findings
fields.description: Main results, conclusions, or claims about how the LLM approach performed or supported urban planning/smart city tasks.
fields.example: The approach improved prediction accuracy and enabled scalable city-wide analysis

fields.name: evaluation_metrics
fields.description: Quantitative or qualitative metrics used to assess performance, such as accuracy, F1, MAE, RMSE, BLEU, human ratings, or task-specific measures.

fields.name: urban_planning_or_smart_city_task
fields.description: The specific urban planning or smart city application addressed by the paper, such as traffic forecasting, noise analysis, land-use planning, mobility, or urban policy support.

fields.name: llm_role
fields.description: How the large language model is used in the study, such as classifier, generator, extractor, planner assistant, evaluator, or reasoning component.
fields.example: LLM used as a scoring and reasoning engine

fields.name: input_data_type
fields.description: The type of input data processed by the LLM-based approach, such as text reports, complaints, sensor time series, maps, policy documents, or multimodal urban data.
fields.example: Urban complaint text and traffic time series

fields.name: comparison_or_baselines
fields.description: Any baseline methods, comparative models, or reference approaches used in the study.
fields.example: Compared against traditional machine learning and non-LLM forecasting models

fields.name: practical_implications
fields.description: Any stated implications for urban planning practice, smart city operations, decision-making, or policy support.
fields.example: Supports scalable city-level monitoring and planning decisions
